emerging_technology: Large-language-model generative AI used by human analysts for bilingual synthesis, public-source market/competitor research and draft market-entry recommendations; no autonomous purchases, negotiation or fieldwork.
industry_sector: Small cross-border management/market-entry consulting practices serving Chinese home/lifestyle consumer brands considering the U.S. market.
users_stakeholders: Chinese brand founders and export/marketing teams; bilingual analysts; U.S. consumers and research participants; channel partners; consulting principals and affected junior staff.
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast follower: consider a reversible, human-reviewed pilot before changing client commitments or staffing.
risk_consequence_context: Incorrect or stale market advice can misallocate client budgets and damage trust; cross-cultural errors, unsupported sources, confidential data leakage and misleading claims are material. No legal/tax/customs/product-compliance advice; refer those decisions to qualified professionals. Management retains approval.
management_question: Over the next 12 months, should management absorb LLM generative AI as an analyst productivity tool, change the paid value proposition, or do both? What evidence would justify the next step?
time_horizon: Decision as of October 13, 2026. Proposed explicit analytical windows: near = now through October 13, 2027; mid = after that through October 13, 2029; far = beyond October 13, 2029. These scenario conventions are not chapter-defined cutoffs or forecasts.
additional_context:

Product category: non-food home/lifestyle consumer goods; exclude regulated-product recommendations and legal, tax, customs or product-compliance advice. Reference date: October 13, 2026. C1 is a conceptual framework, not verified market evidence for this case.

Distinguish a client self-service alternative hypothesis from observed displacement. Do not assume ownership of relationships creates an unassailable moat.
intended_application: Use the identical LLM capability to support public-source research and draft recommendations within a service whose core deliverables are real U.S. customer interviews, field validation, partner diligence and supervised channel-entry execution.
organization: Hypothetical small bilingual consultancy serving the same Chinese home/lifestyle brands, but fieldwork/execution-led rather than report-led.
business_need: Assess whether AI-assisted research complements verified local work or erodes its pricing, and whether to reallocate effort from desk reports to validated execution without assuming relationship advantages guarantee survival.
capabilities_constraints: Assumed baseline: scoped project fees plus ongoing execution retainers; bilingual staff and a U.S. research/partner network; real participant recruitment, interview consent, documented observation and partner follow-up. Reports support rather than constitute the main deliverable. Core costs include fieldwork, coordination and quality review, not only desk analysis. No verified margin, network exclusivity or success rate supplied. Same public/redacted data policy, human sign-off and fast-follower posture as primary. No new AI feature, superior model or extra technical capability is introduced.
